items.text: Neruším? = Am I disturbing you? (on the phone)
items.picture: Split picture of a phone call. Left: Tomáš, at his desk at home in Košice beside his laptop, holds his phone to his ear, a little hesitant. Right: Emma, curled up on her bed in the dorm room with a book, answers with a smile, glad to talk.

items.text: Tomáš calls: “Ahoj, Emma, tu je Tomáš. Neruším?” Emma has time. What does she say?
Nechceš ísť s nami na výlet? = Would you like to come on a trip with us?
items.picture: Split picture of a phone call. Left: Emma, at her desk in the dorm room with a big map of Slovakia spread out in front of her, invites someone on a trip, excited. Right: Marek, on the sofa in his flat, his arm still in a plaster cast and a sling, brightens up at the idea.

items.text: Overím si to. = I'll check.
items.picture: In his flat, Marek, his phone wedged between ear and shoulder, flips through the wall calendar with his good hand to check a date; his other arm is in a plaster cast and a sling.

items.text: Premysli si to. = Think it over.
items.picture: Split picture of a phone call. Left: Emma, phone at her ear, smiles patiently. Right: Marek on his sofa, his arm in a plaster cast, scratches his head with his good hand, undecided.

items.text: Daj mi vedieť. = Let me know.
Vyhovuje ti to? = Does that suit you?
Emma wants to know if Friday suits Marek. What does she ask?
Zatiaľ! = Bye for now! See you!
At the end of the call Marek says “Maj sa!”. What do you answer?
Počujeme sa? = Can you hear me?
items.picture: Split picture of a phone call. Left: Tomáš, in a compartment of the InterCity train with hills rushing past the window, presses his phone to his ear and frowns. Right: Emma, in the dorm kitchen, holds a finger in her other ear, straining to hear him.

items.text: Nepočujem ťa dobre. = I can't hear you well.
Tomáš: “Haló, Emma? Počujeme sa?” The line is bad. What does Emma say?
Prerušilo nás. = We got cut off.
items.picture: Split picture. Left: the train has gone into a dark tunnel, and Tomáš stares at his phone: the call is gone. Right: Emma, in the dorm kitchen, takes her phone from her ear and looks at it, puzzled.

items.text: Volal som pred chvíľou. = I called a moment ago.
To bude asi omyl. = It must be a mistake. (a wrong number)
items.picture: Split picture of a phone call. Left: a hungry man in a tracksuit, on his sofa in front of the TV, phones in his order with a hand on his stomach. Right: Emma, at her dorm desk, listens with raised eyebrows and kindly shakes her head: he's got the wrong number.

items.text: A man calls Emma's mobile: “Haló, je to pizzeria?” What does she say?
The man says: “Prepáčte, pomýlil som sa.” What does Emma answer?
Volané číslo je momentálne nedostupné. = The number you are calling is not available at the moment.
items.picture: Emma, in the dorm kitchen, frowns at her phone as a recorded voice answers instead of Lucia; a bubble shows Lucia's phone lying in her bag, its battery flat and its screen black.

items.text: Emma calls Lucia and hears: “Volané číslo je momentálne nedostupné.” What does it mean?
Nechaj mi odkaz. = Leave me a message.
items.picture: Split picture. Left: in the university library, Lucia studies with big headphones on while her phone buzzes, unnoticed, on the table beside her books. Right: Emma, at a tram stop, phone to her ear, gets ready to leave a message after the beep.

items.text: stážistka = intern (a woman)
items.picture: Emma's first morning as an intern at Tomáš's company: in a smart blazer, with a blank badge on a lanyard round her neck, she arrives at the reception, a little nervous; Petra greets her warmly from behind the desk.

items.text: recepcia = reception
items.picture: The reception at the entrance of Tomáš's company: Petra, at her desk with a phone and a computer, greets a visitor with a smile, while Emma, on a second chair beside her, watches and learns.

items.text: Pri telefóne Emma. = Emma speaking.
items.picture: At the reception desk the phone rings: Emma, sitting up straight, picks it up and answers for the first time, while Petra, beside her, gives her an encouraging thumbs-up.

items.text: The phone rings at reception. What does Emma say?
Môžem hovoriť s pánom Hudákom? = May I speak to Mr Hudák?
items.picture: Split picture of a phone call. Left: a businessman in a suit, at his own office desk, asks for someone. Right: Emma, at the reception phone, glances over her shoulder at pán Hudák, who sits at his desk in his glass-walled corner office.

items.text: S kým chcete hovoriť? = Who would you like to speak to?
Moment, prepojím vás. = One moment, I'll put you through.
items.picture: Emma, the reception phone at her ear, presses a button to put a caller through; through an open office door nearby, the phone on pani Kollárová's desk rings and she reaches for it.

items.text: A caller asks for pani inžinierka Kollárová. She's at her desk. What does Emma say?
pán inžinier, pani inžinierka = Mr …, Mrs … (with an engineer's title)
items.picture: In a corridor at Tomáš's company, Petra introduces Emma to pán Hudák and pani Kollárová: pán Hudák shakes Emma's hand formally, and pani Kollárová smiles beside him.

items.text: Ľutujem, práve má poradu. = I'm sorry, he's in a meeting right now.
items.picture: Split picture of a phone call. Left: a caller, a woman at her own office desk. Right: Emma, at the reception phone, answers apologetically; behind her, through the open door of the meeting room, pán Hudák sits at a table with his colleagues in a meeting.

items.text: Momentálne nie je v kancelárii. = He isn't in the office at the moment.
items.picture: Emma, on the reception phone, looks over at pán Hudák's glass-walled corner office: his desk is empty, his chair pushed back, and his coat is gone from the stand.

items.text: Pán Hudák je tento týždeň na služobnej ceste. What does this mean?
Chcete nechať odkaz? = Would you like to leave a message?
items.picture: At the reception desk, Emma holds the phone to her ear with one hand and has a pen ready over a message pad with the other, listening carefully to the caller.

items.text: Nie, ďakujem, zavolám neskôr. = No, thank you, I'll call back later.
Zavolajte neskôr, prosím. = Please call back later.
Mr Hudák's meeting ends soon. What does Emma tell the caller?
Poviem mu to. = I'll tell him.
items.picture: Pán Hudák, back with his briefcase, stops at the reception desk, and Emma hands him a small handwritten message note; he reads it, nodding.

items.text: Môžem poprosiť ešte raz vaše meno? = Could I have your name again, please?
Emma didn't catch the caller's name. What does she ask?
Reported speech: povedal, že…
Tomáš calls from home: “Mám nejaký odkaz?” (Are there any messages for me?) Which answer is right?
Milá Lucia, = Dear Lucia,
items.picture: Emma, at her dorm desk with a map of Slovakia beside her, types a cheerful e-mail on her laptop; a bubble shows Lucia in the university library reading it on her phone, smiling.

items.text: návrh = suggestion, proposal
items.picture: In the dorm kitchen, Emma spreads a big map of Slovakia across the table and traces a route with her finger; Lucia, Tomáš and Marek, his arm in a sling, lean in, excited.

items.text: Ďakujem Ti za mail. = Thanks for your e-mail.
Pozdravuj Mareka! = Say hi to Marek!
items.picture: Lucia, coat on and a bag of oranges in her hand, heads out of the dorm room to visit her brother; Emma, at her desk, waves after her. A bubble shows Marek on his sofa, his arm in a sling.

items.text: Maj sa dobre! = Take care!
Vážená pani Sokolová, = Dear Mrs Sokolová,
items.picture: Emma, sitting up straight at her dorm desk, writes a careful, formal e-mail on her laptop; a bubble shows pani Sokolová at the small reception desk of her guesthouse in the Tatras, reading it.

items.text: ubytovanie = accommodation
items.picture: Emma and Lucia, side by side at Emma's dorm desk, look at photos of a chalet-style guesthouse with wooden balconies and mountains behind it on the laptop screen.

items.text: voľná izba = a free room, a vacancy
items.picture: At the small reception desk of her guesthouse, pani Sokolová takes one of the last keys off the key rack behind her and holds it up with a smile: there's still a room free.

items.text: Ďakujem za odpoveď. = Thank you for your reply.
S pozdravom = Kind regards
How does Emma end her e-mail to pani Sokolová?
Izba je síce malá, ale pekná. = The room may be small, but it's nice.
items.picture: A small bedroom under the sloping roof of the guesthouse: barely room for two pine beds and a little table, but cosy, with a checked quilt, flowers on the windowsill and the mountain peaks outside the window.

items.text: Dobrý deň, dve dvojposteľové izby Vám rezervujem na meno Šimková. Izba stojí tridsať eur na noc, aj s raňajkami. V. Sokolová Pani Sokolová's reply. How much is a room?
Milí kamaráti, výlet je od piatku do pondelka. Ideme autom. Ubytovanie: penzión, tri noci s raňajkami. Trasa je v prílohe. Emma Emma's e-mail to her friends. What's true?
osobné údaje = personal details
formulár = form
adresa = address
Meno: Emma. Miesto narodenia: Dublin. Povolanie: študentka. Adresa: Javorová 12, Bratislava. Emma's form. Where was she born?
prihlásiť sa = to sign up, to register
Vážený pán inžinier, = Dear Sir, (to a man with an engineer's title)
príloha = attachment
esemeska = text message
items.picture: Emma, on a bench in the sunny university courtyard, types a text message with both thumbs, grinning.

items.text: Budem meškať. = I'll be late.
items.picture: Emma stands in a crowded tram stuck in traffic, glancing anxiously at her watch while she types a text with one hand.

items.text: Emma is still on the tram, and she's meeting Lucia at five. What does she text?
Nestíham. = I can't make it. / I'm running late.
Musím zrušiť stretnutie. = I have to cancel our meeting.
items.picture: Split picture. Left: Tomáš, a laptop under his arm, about to walk into a meeting at his company, quickly types a text. Right: Emma, waiting at a table in the café near the university, reads it on her phone, and her face falls.

items.text: Ahoj, dnes nestíham, mám poradu. Hneváš sa? Môžeme sa stretnúť zajtra. Pekný deň! T. A text from Tomáš. What does he want?
Stíhaš to o piatej? A text from Lucia. What is she asking?
Marek texts: “Kino o ôsmej?” Which answer says yes?
Lucia has a cold. What does Emma tell her?
items.picture: In the dorm room, Lucia sits in bed with a cold, a red nose and a box of tissues on her knees; Emma hands her a big steaming mug of tea.

items.text: A cat walks into the office kitchen and wants your lunch. What do you tell it?
items.picture: In the small office kitchen at Tomáš's company, a cat that has wandered in sits on the table, eyeing Emma's open lunch box; Emma, coming back from the coffee machine with a cup, stops in her tracks.

items.text: list = letter
items.picture: At her dorm desk, Emma folds a handwritten letter to her mum and addresses an envelope, a photo of her family propped against the lamp.

items.text: balík = parcel
items.picture: In the post office, a long counter with scales and racks of envelopes, Emma heaves a big parcel onto the scales while the clerk, a cheerful grey-haired man, checks the weight. A bubble shows Emma's mum at home in Ireland opening the same parcel, delighted.

items.text: Koľko stojí známka do Írska? = How much is a stamp to Ireland?
items.picture: At the post office counter, the cheerful grey-haired clerk tears a stamp off a sheet for Emma, who holds out her letter in its envelope.

items.text: obálka = envelope
adresát a odosielateľ = addressee and sender
At the post office: Emma wants to send a parcel to Ireland. What does she say?
How do you write Emma's address on an envelope?
On a parcel, who is the odosielateľ?
Which opening fits an e-mail to Mrs Sokolová?
Lucia wants to call Tomáš, but he's in a meeting. What do you tell her?
